common_name: Lanai Blue Verbena (Blue-Purple Low-Trailing Spiller Verbena)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in full sun; this low, flat-trailing Lanai selection works best as a spiller along container edges or as a flowering groundcover.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil or container mix after the last frost, spacing plants to let the flat, low-growing stems knit together into a solid carpet of blue-purple blooms. Lanai Blue flowers continuously from planting through hard frost without deadheading and tolerates heat and short dry spells once established. Its trailing habit makes it a dependable spiller for hanging baskets and window boxes as well as a flowering edging plant, and it draws butterflies through the season.

common_name: Lanai Bright Pink Verbena (Vivid Pink Trailing Spiller Verbena)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun with sharp drainage; US Plant Patent 13,982 covers this older, reliable Lanai color.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained soil or potting mix, watering when the top inch dries rather than on a fixed schedule. Lanai Bright Pink opens vivid pink flower clusters over a compact, flat-trailing mound, blooming from planting until the first hard frost with no deadheading required. It performs well as a spiller in mixed containers and hanging baskets and tolerates heat and brief drought once roots are established.

common_name: Lanai Red Verbena (True Red Low-Trailing Verbena)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 18,986 covers this ground-hugging red-flowered Lanai selection.

directions: Site in full sun in well-drained garden soil or container mix after the last frost; Lanai Red stays under six inches tall while spreading into a flat mat of true-red flower clusters. It blooms from planting through the first hard frost without deadheading and holds up well to summer heat and short dry spells. Use it as a groundcover edging, spiller in baskets, or filler among taller sun annuals.

common_name: Lanai White Verbena (Pure White Trailing Spiller Verbena)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun with good drainage; the pure white flowers brighten mixed plantings and show well against darker-flowered companions.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained soil or container mix, allowing the flat, trailing stems room to spread into neighboring plantings. Lanai White covers itself in clean white flower clusters continuously from planting to hard frost and needs no deadheading to keep flowering. It is heat tolerant and useful as a cooling color break between brighter Lanai or Superbena colors in mixed beds and baskets.

common_name: Luscious Basket Tangeglow Lantana (Peach-Orange-and-Yellow Mounding Basket Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; this Luscious selection was bred with hanging baskets in mind, with blooms that spill cleanly over container edges.

directions: Site in full sun in well-drained soil or hanging basket mix after the last frost; Luscious Basket Tangeglow mounds and spills with clusters of peach, orange, and yellow flowers that bloom continuously without deadheading. It tolerates heat and drought once established and keeps flowering through a long, hot summer. Its looser, cascading habit suits hanging baskets and window boxes as well as landscape beds.

common_name: Luscious Berry Blend Lantana (Fuchsia-to-Orange-and-Yellow Multicolor Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 23,919 covers this multicolor Luscious selection.

directions: Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil after the last frost; Luscious Berry Blend forms a dense mound topped with flower clusters that shift from fuchsia to orange and yellow within each head. It blooms without interruption from planting through hard frost, needs no deadheading, and shrugs off heat and short dry spells once rooted in. Birds, butterflies, and hummingbirds are drawn to its clustered, multicolor blooms.

common_name: Luscious Goldengate Lantana (Compact Golden-Yellow Mounding Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 32,224 covers this solid golden-yellow Luscious release.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil after the last frost, giving plants room to mound to their full size. Luscious Goldengate carries solid golden-yellow flower clusters nonstop from planting to frost without deadheading, and holds up to heat and drought better than many older landscape lantanas. It attracts butterflies and hummingbirds and generally resists deer browsing.

common_name: Luscious Grape Lantana (Deep Purple Trailing Weeping Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 19,357 covers this trailing weeping lantana, bred for a brighter purple than older Trailing Lavender types.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, where trailing stems can cascade over a wall, raised bed, or container edge, extending to three feet or more as they mature. Luscious Grape covers itself in purple flowers through hot, humid summer weather and keeps blooming without deadheading. Lightly fragrant foliage adds another layer of interest, and the plant tolerates drought well once its roots are established.

common_name: Luscious Marmalade Lantana (Bright Orange Mounding Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 27,378 covers this orange-flowered Luscious selection.

directions: Site in full sun in average, well-drained soil after the last frost; Luscious Marmalade mounds to two feet or more and opens bright orange flower clusters with yellow highlights that deepen slightly as they age. It reblooms continuously from planting through frost with no deadheading needed and tolerates heat and short dry spells once established. The vivid orange color pairs well with blue or purple companions in mixed beds.

common_name: Luscious Pinkberry Blend Lantana (Pink-Yellow-and-Cream Multicolor Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 28,175 covers this multicolor Luscious selection, a Penn State University top-performer selection.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained soil after the last frost; Luscious Pinkberry Blend forms a mounding, later trailing plant covered in flower clusters that mix pink, yellow, and cream tones with a light, sweet fragrance. It blooms continuously with minimal seed set and needs no deadheading, tolerating heat and drought once rooted in. Butterflies, hummingbirds, and songbirds are regular visitors, while deer generally leave it alone.

common_name: Luscious Royale Cosmo Lantana (Magenta-Purple with Yellow-Orange Highlights Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; this Royale-line selection sets small, tightly packed magenta-purple flower clusters against dark foliage.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, where its dark foliage sets off puffs of magenta-purple flowers highlighted with yellow-orange. Luscious Royale Cosmo blooms continuously from planting through the first hard frost and needs no deadheading to keep producing color. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and works equally well in landscape beds and large containers.

common_name: Luscious Royale Lemon Tart Lantana (Vibrant Lemon-Yellow Mounding Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 33,965 covers this lemon-yellow Royale-line Luscious selection.

directions: Site in full sun in well-drained soil after the last frost; Luscious Royale Lemon Tart produces clusters of bright lemon-yellow flowers from spring through frost over a dense, mounded habit. It flowers continuously without deadheading and tolerates heat well once established, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds throughout the season. Use it in beds, borders, or containers where a clear, saturated yellow is wanted.

common_name: Luscious Royale Red Zone Lantana (True Red Mounding Lantana)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun; US Plant Patent 33,116 covers this true-red Royale-line Luscious selection, bred at the University of Florida.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, spacing plants to fill in as a dense mound. Luscious Royale Red Zone opens clustered true-red flowers continuously from planting through hard frost without deadheading, tolerating heat and drought once rooted in. Birds, butterflies, and hummingbirds visit regularly, and plants generally resist deer browsing.

common_name: Profusion Cherry Bicolor Zinnia (Pink-and-White Bicolor Disease-Resistant Single Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; this bicolor Profusion sibling pairs pink and white on each flower, distinct from the solid-colored Profusion Cherry.

directions: Direct sow or set out transplants after the last frost in full sun; Profusion Cherry Bicolor opens single, daisy-form flowers combining pink and white across each bloom on compact, mounded plants. Like other Profusion-series selections it blooms continuously without deadheading and carries strong resistance to the powdery mildew and leaf spot that trouble older zinnia varieties in humid summers. Its dense, weather-resistant habit suits beds, borders, and containers with minimal upkeep beyond occasional light feeding.

common_name: Magellan Cherry Zinnia (Compact Large-Flowered Cherry-Red Dahlia-Type Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; the compact Magellan series stays shorter and more uniform than older tall dahlia-flowered zinnias.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or set out transplants in full sun; Magellan Cherry forms a compact, upright plant topped with large, fully double, cherry-red dahlia-form flowers from summer through fall. Its short, uniform habit needs no staking and holds up well in containers as well as garden beds. Heat and drought tolerant once established, it keeps flowering with only occasional grooming.

common_name: Magellan Ivory Zinnia (Compact Large-Flowered Creamy-White Dahlia-Type Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; the soft ivory tone pairs easily with brighter Magellan colors in mixed plantings.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Magellan Ivory carries large, fully double creamy-white flowers on a compact, self-supporting plant from summer into fall. The short Magellan habit needs no staking and performs well in containers, borders, and cutting gardens alike. It tolerates heat and brief drought once established, with minimal care beyond occasional grooming.

common_name: Magellan Mix Zinnia (Compact Large-Flowered Multicolor Dahlia-Type Zinnia Blend)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; this blend mixes the full range of Magellan series colors on uniformly compact plants.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or set out transplants in full sun; Magellan Mix combines orange, pink, purple, red, white, and yellow dahlia-form flowers across a planting of equally compact, uniform plants. The short habit needs no staking and performs reliably in beds, borders, and containers. Heat and drought tolerant once rooted in, it blooms from summer through fall with little maintenance.

common_name: Magellan Scarlet Zinnia (Compact Large-Flowered Scarlet Dahlia-Type Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; the saturated scarlet color holds well in bright summer light.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Magellan Scarlet produces large, fully double scarlet-red flowers on a short, upright, self-supporting plant. Like the rest of the Magellan series it stays uniform and compact without staking, making it useful as a filler in beds and containers. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and attracts butterflies through a long summer-to-fall bloom season.

common_name: Magellan Yellow Zinnia (Compact Large-Flowered Golden-Yellow Dahlia-Type Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; bright yellow blooms make this a strong anchor color in the Magellan line.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Magellan Yellow bears large, fully double golden-yellow flowers over a short, uniform plant that needs no staking. It flowers from summer through fall, tolerating heat and brief drought once established, and draws butterflies into the garden. Its compact habit fits containers and landscape beds equally well.

common_name: Sweet Tooth Candy Cane Zinnia (Compact Candy-Striped Sweet Tooth Series Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; this is a newer Sweet Tooth series color distinct from the older Magellan and Profusion lines.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Sweet Tooth Candy Cane holds a compact, upright habit and flowers prolifically from planting until frost. It is heat and drought tolerant once established, needing little more than occasional light feeding to keep producing blooms. Use it as a filler in sunny containers and landscape beds alongside other Sweet Tooth series colors.

common_name: Sweet Tooth Candy Corn Zinnia (Compact Red-and-Yellow Sweet Tooth Series Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; blooms open red at the center and shade to yellow at the tips.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Sweet Tooth Candy Corn opens red-and-yellow flowers on a compact, upright plant that blooms from planting through frost without a break. It tolerates heat and drought once established and keeps a tidy, self-supporting habit that needs no staking. The two-tone bloom reads well in containers, cutting gardens, and mixed sunny borders.

common_name: Sweet Tooth Cotton Candy Zinnia (Compact Pink Sweet Tooth Series Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; soft pink blooms make this a gentle companion to the brighter Sweet Tooth colors.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Sweet Tooth Cotton Candy bears large, soft pink flowers on a compact, upright plant from planting through frost. It is heat and drought tolerant once established and requires little beyond occasional feeding to keep flowering steadily. Its tidy habit suits containers and mixed garden beds in full sun.

common_name: Sweet Tooth Lemonhead Zinnia (Compact Yellow Sweet Tooth Series Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; a prolific bloomer well suited to filling out containers.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Sweet Tooth Lemonhead flowers prolifically on a compact, upright plant from planting until frost. Growers note its reliable, filled-out container performance thanks to its even, self-supporting habit. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and needs little care beyond occasional feeding.

common_name: Sweet Tooth Licorice Zinnia (Compact Deep Burgundy Sweet Tooth Series Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; the deep, near-black tone adds contrast among lighter Sweet Tooth colors.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Sweet Tooth Licorice stays compact and upright while flowering from planting through frost. Its deep, dark bloom color offers a strong accent against the Sweet Tooth series' lighter pastel and bright shades. It is heat and drought tolerant once established and suits both containers and landscape plantings.

common_name: Sweet Tooth Orange Slice Zinnia (Compact Orange Sweet Tooth Series Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after the last frost into full sun; a solid orange filler color for the Sweet Tooth series.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost or transplant into full sun; Sweet Tooth Orange Slice carries its bright orange flowers over a compact, upright plant from planting to frost. It functions well as a filler in sunny containers and borders, holding a tidy, self-supporting habit without staking. Heat and drought tolerant once established, it needs only occasional light feeding to keep flowering steadily.
